profile.campus: Data4 MIL01 campus, Cornaredo, Milan (217 MW / 20 ha campus total, distinct from the separate MIL02 site in Vittuone)

source.basis: Operator campus page, structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading:
DCL09 is one building mapped on the DATA4 campus that the Italian environmental file calls the D4 Digital Campus and that DATA4 sells as MIL01. One caution belongs on this row before anything else. The ministry file's geotechnical schedule names buildings DC01 through DC10 plus the twin towers DC08.1 and DC08.2, and groups DC09 with DC06, DC07 and DC10 on an older layer of fill. It does not use a DCL prefix anywhere. No DATA4 or ministry document reviewed explains the DCL naming used in this registry's source data, so whether DCL09 corresponds to the ministry's DC09, to a later building not yet named in the ministry file, or to something else, is not established here. That uncertainty is the one specific fact this row can state about the building itself.

DATA4 is a European colocation developer and operator headquartered in Paris. Its group pages describe ten campuses across France, Italy, Spain, Poland, Germany and Greece, sixteen data centres in operation, around 165,000 square metres of IT space, roughly 1.5 GW of available energy capacity and about 200 hectares of land reserve. Ownership has moved more than once. Brookfield acquired the business, and on 1 August 2025 DATA4 announced that Arjun Infrastructure Partners and Interogo Holding had taken a significant stake in a stabilised portfolio of hyperscale sites in Paris, Milan and Madrid carrying a combined contracted capacity of 244 MW. Older DATA4 material describing control by AXA is superseded. The Italian entities in the public file are DATA 4 MILAN S.p.A., proponent of the environmental assessment, and DATA 4 ITALY S.p.A. of Piazza Eleonora Duse 2 in Milan, named on the drawings.

The campus occupies flat irrigated plain roughly fifteen kilometres west of central Milan, on the boundary between the comuni of Cornaredo and Settimo Milanese, with the Settimo Milanese half standing on the former Italtel industrial estate on Via Guglielmo Reiss Romoli. The environmental file divides it into lots. Lot A, the campus plot, covers about 20,000 square metres in Cornaredo and about 60,000 in Settimo Milanese and holds ten completed buildings plus an administrative building, the water reserve, the high voltage cabin and an external generator set. Lot B, the Verdi Tower plot, holds the twin buildings DC08.1 and DC08.2 under construction. The canteen lots C1 and C2 measure 17,972 and 22,642 square metres. Lot D, the Villa Cascina plot, carries the historic Villa Litta-Modignani and is where a new substation is to be built. The reason for the location is interconnection. This is the Milan metropolitan hub, and DATA4 lists dedicated points of presence for the Milan Internet Exchange and for TOP-IX on campus, with access to more than seventy telecom operators and over 150 public cloud platforms.

DATA4 has never broken its campus capacity down by building and the ministry file does not do it either, so no power or area figure is recorded against this building individually. The campus numbers, and which of them is load and which is not, are in campus_power_note. The short form is that 170 MW is a campus capacity figure that DATA4 does not call IT load, that the campus is served by an existing 57 MW substation with a 100 MW one planned, and that the 701.44 MWt figure in the ministry file is the thermal input rating of the standby diesel fleet, not electrical output.

The campus carries an unusually full public record. It is the subject of a retrospective environmental impact assessment at the national environment ministry, opened in December 2024 and still in technical examination, and of a separate application for an integrated environmental authorisation lodged in February 2026 for the two canteen lots, both set out in regulatory_note. The local record, including the Parco Agricolo Sud Milano's formal opinion and the rejected moratorium motion in the Cornaredo council, is in community_note.

What is not known matters here, and for this row it starts with the building's own identity. Beyond that, DATA4 publishes no IT load figure for the campus or for any building on it, and no floor area per building. No tenant is named anywhere in the public record. The PUE, projected electricity and water consumption, and the rating of the rooftop photovoltaic arrays that the ministry asked DATA4 to specify were answered in a separate decarbonisation annex that could not be retrieved, so none of those numbers is asserted.
profile.capacity_note: Campus level total published, 170 MW and 20 hectares, not broken down per building, so no per building MW or square footage figure is recorded.

profile.community_note: The local record is contested and well documented. The Parco Agricolo Sud Milano, which manages the protected agricultural belt immediately south and east of the site, filed a formal opinion registered at the ministry on 22 July 2025 asking for heavier landscape mitigation along those two edges and for a co ordinated environmental project agreed with both comuni and with the park. Its closing passage reaches beyond this site, arguing that new data centres are now among the main consumers of open land in the Milan metropolitan area, that the electrical substations they require are often built without proper planning, and that hyperscale infrastructure needs siting decisions taken at a wide scale with preference for derelict industrial land. In Cornaredo the Partito Democratico moved for an immediate suspension of permits and authorisations for new data centres. The council rejected the motion, the mayor arguing that a moratorium would conflict with the comune's own Piano di Governo del Territorio, which treats data centres as compatible with the productive zones it designates, and would expose the comune to legal claims. A separate motion from the Il Colibri Sinistra per Cornaredo list asked instead for binding local criteria covering acoustic modelling, visual simulation with photo simulations, renewable sourcing and community consultation. Mitigation agreed with the two comuni includes 437 trees and improvement works on the local fontanili, the spring fed watercourses that characterise this plain.
profile.regulatory_note: The campus is the subject of two separate national procedures at the Ministero dell'Ambiente e della Sicurezza Energetica. The first is an environmental impact assessment, ID_VIP 13540, online code VIAVIA100000067, titled Progetto D4 Data Center MIL1 - Masterplan campus, proponent DATA 4 MILAN S.p.A., covering Settimo Milanese and Cornaredo and classified under the heading Centrali. It was lodged on 27 December 2024 and converted into a VIA postuma, a retrospective assessment under article 29 of D.Lgs. 152/2006, for a campus the file itself describes as in part already built. Documents were perfected on 27 May 2025, public consultation ran from 6 June to 5 August 2025, the ministry requested additions on 20 October 2025 and received them on 17 November 2025, a second consultation ran from 1 December to 31 December 2025, and the file was republished a second time on 14 April 2026 with observations open to 14 May 2026. The ministry then asked for further perfection of the papers by note protocol 119318 of 5 June 2026. Status is technical examination by the CTVIA. The second procedure is an application for an integrated environmental authorisation, AIA, ID 11998, filed under MASE protocol 22222 on 3 February 2026 for lots C and D of the MIL01 campus in Cornaredo, with public consultation from 26 February to 28 March 2026 and the installation recorded as not yet built. Municipal consents referenced in the file sit with the Comune di Settimo Milanese, including practice 19/2025 for DC08.1, practice 7/2025 handled as a SCIA in place of a building permit, and practice 3/2025 lodged under protocol 29375 on 16 October 2025 for the landscape impact review of the 100 MW substation.
profile.campus_power_note: The four power numbers for this campus have to be kept apart, because the largest published figure is not load of any kind. DATA4's own Milan location page gives the MIL01 campus 170 MW. That is a campus level available capacity figure and DATA4 never calls it IT load, so it is not recorded as one, and an earlier 217 MW value carried in this profile is not supported by DATA4's current page. The ministry file shows the electrical infrastructure the campus figure rests on. An existing on site substation appears in the geotechnical schedule as SS 57 MW, and a new 100 MW transformer substation, the SSE, is to be built on the Villa Cascina lot to feed the data centres planned for canteen lots C1 and C2. Those are grid and transformation ratings for the whole campus, not for any one building, so no per building utility figure is recorded. The 701.44 MWt in the ministry file is the number most likely to be misread. It is the combined thermal input rating of the standby diesel generator fleet, and it is what pushed the project past the 150 MW thermal threshold in Allegato II to Part Two of D.Lgs. 152/2006 and so into a state level environmental assessment. It is fuel heat input for emergency plant, not electrical output, not grid capacity and not IT load. For scale, the generator set serving Lot A alone is rated 16.30 MWt. No IT load figure, for the campus or for any building on it, appears in any DATA4 or ministry document reviewed.
